summary: Six tests pass only in the main checkout because they read gitignored, untracked research artifacts or raw data through repo-relative paths. In any fresh worktree (which by policy holds no data/ and no study _work/ or model artifacts) they fail, and test_delta classifies them NEW_FAILURE instead of ENVIRONMENTAL_MISSING_ARTIFACT.

tests.tests/test_catalog_materializer.py::test: data/raw/YM_v0_1s_2024.parquet (resolved under the checkout, not via catalog_roots)

evidence: each passes on main f2b748c4 (where the gitignored file exists) and fails in the chore worktree (where it does not); the chore touched none of their code paths
two_defects: the tests hard-depend on untracked artifacts without a skip/explicit environmental classification
scripts/test_delta.py ENVIRONMENTAL_MISSING_ARTIFACT did not recognise these FileNotFoundError / model-artifact-missing / RAW_DATA_MISSING failures (counted 0)
prohibited_workaround: copying or linking gitignored research artifacts or raw data into a worktree to make these pass (undocumented, and links are blocked by scripts/hooks/data_guard.py)
fix_direction_not_implemented: a bounded chore: either mark each test to skip with an explicit environmental reason when its artifact is absent (as test_runtime_bindings already does for compiled_study.json), or resolve data through the configured catalog/artifact roots; and teach test_delta to classify the missing-artifact signatures as ENVIRONMENTAL_MISSING_ARTIFACT
